name: OroCommerce
title: OroCommerce SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce Connector
description: Svelte Commerce on OroCommerce’s storefront JSON:API: 21 of 43 services wired, with cart, checkout and sign-in. No cash on delivery. Setup and fixes.
lede: OroCommerce’s storefront API speaks JSON:API, and the connector ships a deserialiser that resolves `included` relationships. Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; reviews, wishlist, currencies and vendors are the gaps.
verdict: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; reviews, wishlist, currencies and vendors are not. There is no cash on delivery — OroCommerce has no such payment method — so orders go through Oro’s PayPal Express or Stripe checkout.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your OroCommerce website

env.name: PUBLIC_OROCOMMERCE_API_URL
env.note: The website origin: the storefront JSON:API lives at `{url}/api` and the token endpoint at `{url}/oauth2-token`. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_OROCOMMERCE_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.note: Sent as a bearer token when set.

env.name: PUBLIC_OROCOMMERCE_LOCALIZATION_ID
env.note: Sent as `X-Localization-ID`: the locale every localised field comes back in.

env.name: PUBLIC_OROCOMMERCE_CURRENCY
env.note: Sent as `X-Currency`. OroCommerce Enterprise only; Community Edition ignores it.

env.name: PUBLIC_OROCOMMERCE_PRODUCT_ID_MODE
env.note: `sku` addresses products by SKU instead of numeric ID, sent as `X-Product-ID: sku` on every request.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/orocommerce-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: `init.ts` hands the connector every `PUBLIC_OROCOMMERCE_*` variable that is set, camel-cased. The guide also lists `PUBLIC_OROCOMMERCE_STORE_ID` and `PUBLIC_OROCOMMERCE_CHANNEL_ID`, which Oro ignores — it resolves the website from the request’s host — and `PUBLIC_OROCOMMERCE_ACCESS_KEY`, which the connector’s source does not read.
backendSettings: Create an OAuth application for the storefront API; its client ID and secret go in `PUBLIC_OROCOMMERCE_API_KEY` and `PUBLIC_OROCOMMERCE_API_SECRET` — read the limitations first.
Configure PayPal Express or Stripe on the Oro side if shoppers are to pay: OroCommerce has no cash-on-delivery method, and the storefront’s cash-on-delivery option throws.
howItWorks: Oro’s storefront API answers in JSON:API, and the connector resolves `included` relationships with its own deserialiser (the `jsonapi` file in its source is that helper, not a service). The website is resolved from the request’s host; locale, currency and SKU addressing travel as Oro’s documented headers. Payment goes through Oro’s checkout endpoints for PayPal Express and Stripe.
limitations: No cash on delivery: OroCommerce has no such payment method, so the storefront’s cash-on-delivery option throws `NotSupportedError`.
The OAuth client ID and secret come from `PUBLIC_OROCOMMERCE_API_KEY` and `PUBLIC_OROCOMMERCE_API_SECRET`. SvelteKit sends `PUBLIC_` variables to the browser, so every visitor can read them.

faq.q: Can I run an OroCommerce store on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; reviews, wishlist, currencies and vendors are not, and there is no cash on delivery. Like every connector, it has not been run against a live production OroCommerce store.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to OroCommerce?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/orocommerce-connector`, set `PUBLIC_OROCOMMERCE_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: How do shoppers pay on OroCommerce?
faq.a: Through Oro’s own checkout endpoints for PayPal Express and Stripe. OroCommerce has no cash-on-delivery payment method, so that option in the storefront throws rather than pretend.

api.surface: The connector calls OroCommerce’s storefront JSON:API under `{apiUrl}/api`, sending `application/vnd.api+json` as both `Accept` and `Content-Type`, and stays off the back-office API at `/admin/api`, whose tokens it treats as not interchangeable.
api.auth: Every request carries `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` from an OAuth2 password grant on `{apiUrl}/oauth2-token` (outside `/api`, plain JSON, with `client_id` and `client_secret` from the API key and secret); an anonymous shopper gets a visitor token from the same grant with the literal username and password `guest`, a signed-in customer user gets one with their email and password, and both tokens are kept in the `oro_access_token` and `oro_refresh_token` cookies and refreshed once on a 401.

calls.what: `GET /api/mastercatalogtree?include=category` for the whole tree; `GET /api/products?filter[rootCategory]={id}` for a category’s products
`POST /api/shoppinglists/{id}/checkout` to start; `GET /api/checkouts/{id}/availableShippingMethods` and `availablePaymentMethods`; `PATCH /api/checkouts/{id}` to set the methods
`GET /api/checkouts/{id}/payment`, then `POST` to the `meta.paymentUrl` it returns; `POST /api/checkouts/{id}/paymentPayPalExpress` or `paymentStripePaymentElement` when that gateway is asked for
`GET /api/orders` with `include=lineItems,status` and `filter[identifier]` for an order number; `GET /api/orders/{id}`

rules: Oro’s storefront API has no `meta.totalCount` and no `Link` header, so every paged read sends `X-Include: totalCount` and reads the total from the `X-Include-Total-Count` response header.

The cart is a shopping list, addressed by the literal id `default`, which Oro resolves on the server to the current visitor’s or customer user’s list; the connector caches no cart id, so a sign-in or sign-out never points at the previous session’s list.
At sign-in the connector forwards the stored visitor token as `visitor_access_token`, which is what moves the guest’s shopping list onto the customer user.
A product or category slug is resolved through `GET /api/routes/{id}`, whose id is the storefront path with every slash replaced by a colon, so `/products/medical` becomes `:products:medical`.
Product sorting is limited to `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `id` and `sku`, because Oro answers any other sorter with a 400; an unknown sort falls back to `-id`.
